GracePrinciples.Principle: Contract-first changes: establish module ownership, public vocabulary, and verification evidence before implementation.
API-owned state is authoritative; adapters own presentation and recovery state, while workers own execution mechanics only.
Semantic anchors remain stable, grep-friendly, attribute-free tag names; every module has one graph owner and one derived verification entry.
Immutable snapshots and fenced lifecycle transitions protect retries, cancellation, publication, delivery, and retention from races.
Use fresh assertions, focused tests, deterministic fixtures, disposable database resets, and runtime smoke checks as completion evidence.
Preserve diagnostics and provenance for failures; do not claim historical commands were rerun when migrating evidence.
Do not create retroactive change bundles during migration; historical packets remain recoverable in the approved external backup and Git history.
Build bottom-up: contracts and disposable storage reset, then API domain/orchestration, workers, adapters, deterministic coverage, and final runtime/readiness proof.

Deploy additive forward-only schema and disabled consumers before enabling claims, adapters, retention reconciliation, and physical deletion; rollback disables claims and drains leases without destructive Down migrations.

Definition of done requires canonical contracts, current module/verification routing, focused automated tests, no-legacy guards, clean compose configuration, live runtime evidence where claimed, and tracked residual risk.
Configuration belongs to infrastructure/runtime environment; durable media, lifecycle, diagnostics, and presentation-recovery state belongs to API product storage.
